title: How a Water Tower Supplies an Entire Neighbourhood

beats.narration: If you connect one house to a pump, water comes out of the tap. Easy.

beats.problem: More houses demand water at the same time.
beats.narration: But now six more families turn on their taps, and demand shoots up.

beats.problem: Supply needs enough energy to reach the network.
beats.narration: So you install a bigger pumping station to move treated water into the system.
But demand changes all day. Running pumps alone makes the supply harder to balance.
So you build an enormous tank high above the streets, then pump water into it.

beats.problem: Water must reach taps over a wider area.
beats.narration: Now the height of the water creates pressure. Gravity drives it through underground mains.

beats.problem: Every home needs a branch connection.
beats.narration: Those mains branch out, delivering water to houses across the neighbourhood.
The pumps refill the tank. Congratulations, you've built a water tower.
